**Santa Rosa County** is a county in the northwestern portion of the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The county seat is Milton, which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the Pensacola metropolitan area, which also includes Escambia County.

The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of Tristan de Luna's failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission serving Apalachees, Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in Floridatown from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)
Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint Rosa de Viterbo.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)
Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)
Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 1,174 square miles (3,040 km 2), of which 162 sq mi (420 km 2) (13.8%) are covered by water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR1-7)

### National protected area
[edit]
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part)
Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.
Navarre Beach
South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the Fairpoint Peninsula, and along U.S. Highway 98. A section of Santa Rosa Island, containing the unincorporated community of Navarre Beach, is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for Pensacola to the west and Hurlburt Field, Fort Walton Beach, and Eglin Air Force Base to the east.
Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called Old Spanish Trail that ran from St. Augustine to New Orleans, and further points west. Today, U.S. Highway 90 closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional Southern culture. The Pace and Milton communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. Interstate 10 also passes through this section of the county. The U.S. Navy presence is marked by Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.

### National protected area
Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along State Road 4, which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.
State Road 87 traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with Escambia County, Alabama, near Brewton, where it connects with State Route 41. This road is a primary emergency evacuation route for the county during hurricanes.

### Board of county commissioners
[edit]
The Santa Rosa County Board of County Commissioners serves as the legislative and policy-setting body of the county as established under Chapter 125 of the Florida Statutes. As such, the board enacts all legislation and authorizes programs and expenditures within the county. The board appoints a professionally trained county administrator, who is responsible for policy and budget development and implementation.
The board comprises five members, elected countywide. Members must reside within the particular districts for which they seek election. Each year, the board organizes itself, selecting a chair and vice chair from among its members to preside at commission meetings.

As of the 2020 census, 188,000 people, 69,454 households, and 47,876 families resided in the county.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
The median age was 40.3 years; 22.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 16.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 103.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 102.1 males age 18 and over.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### Racial and ethnic composition
The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% White, 5.9% Black or African American, 0.7% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.1% Asian, 0.2% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)
Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)
There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### Racial and ethnic composition
As of the 2000 census,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The population density was 116 inhabitants per square mile (45/km 2). The 49,119 housing units had an average density of 48 per square mile (19/km 2). The racial makeup of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% Native American, 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.
Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.
In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

### Racial and ethnic composition
The median income for a household in the county was $41,881 and for a family was $46,929. Males had a median income of $34,878 versus $22,304 for females. The per capita income for the county was $20,089. About 7.9% of families and 9.8% of the population were below the poverty line, including 12.6% of those under 18 and 7.5% of those 65 or over.

**Santa Rosa County** is a county in the northwestern portion of the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The county seat is Milton, which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the Pensacola metropolitan area, which also includes Escambia County.
texts.1:
The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of Tristan de Luna's failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission serving Apalachees, Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in Floridatown from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)
Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint Rosa de Viterbo.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)
Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)
Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 1,174 square miles (3,040 km 2), of which 162 sq mi (420 km 2) (13.8%) are covered by water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR1-7)

### National protected area
[edit]
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part)
Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.
Navarre Beach
South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the Fairpoint Peninsula, and along U.S. Highway 98. A section of Santa Rosa Island, containing the unincorporated community of Navarre Beach, is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for Pensacola to the west and Hurlburt Field, Fort Walton Beach, and Eglin Air Force Base to the east.
Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called Old Spanish Trail that ran from St. Augustine to New Orleans, and further points west. Today, U.S. Highway 90 closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional Southern culture. The Pace and Milton communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. Interstate 10 also passes through this section of the county. The U.S. Navy presence is marked by Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.
texts.3:
### National protected area
Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along State Road 4, which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.
State Road 87 traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with Escambia County, Alabama, near Brewton, where it connects with State Route 41. This road is a primary emergency evacuation route for the county during hurricanes.

### Board of county commissioners
[edit]
The Santa Rosa County Board of County Commissioners serves as the legislative and policy-setting body of the county as established under Chapter 125 of the Florida Statutes. As such, the board enacts all legislation and authorizes programs and expenditures within the county. The board appoints a professionally trained county administrator, who is responsible for policy and budget development and implementation.
The board comprises five members, elected countywide. Members must reside within the particular districts for which they seek election. Each year, the board organizes itself, selecting a chair and vice chair from among its members to preside at commission meetings.

### Racial and ethnic composition
The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% White, 5.9% Black or African American, 0.7% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.1% Asian, 0.2% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)
Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)
There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

As of the 2000 census,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The population density was 116 inhabitants per square mile (45/km 2). The 49,119 housing units had an average density of 48 per square mile (19/km 2). The racial makeup of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% Native American, 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.
Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.
In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

**Santa Rosa County** is a county in the northwestern portion of the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The county seat is Milton, which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the Pensacola metropolitan area, which also includes Escambia County.

The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of Tristan de Luna's failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission serving Apalachees, Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in Floridatown from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)
Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint Rosa de Viterbo.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)
Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)
Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 1,174 square miles (3,040 km 2), of which 162 sq mi (420 km 2) (13.8%) are covered by water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR1-7)

### National protected area
[edit]
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part)
Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.
Navarre Beach
South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the Fairpoint Peninsula, and along U.S. Highway 98. A section of Santa Rosa Island, containing the unincorporated community of Navarre Beach, is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for Pensacola to the west and Hurlburt Field, Fort Walton Beach, and Eglin Air Force Base to the east.
Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called Old Spanish Trail that ran from St. Augustine to New Orleans, and further points west. Today, U.S. Highway 90 closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional Southern culture. The Pace and Milton communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. Interstate 10 also passes through this section of the county. The U.S. Navy presence is marked by Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.

### National protected area
Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along State Road 4, which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.
State Road 87 traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with Escambia County, Alabama, near Brewton, where it connects with State Route 41. This road is a primary emergency evacuation route for the county during hurricanes.
*   Escambia County, Alabama - north  
*   Okaloosa County, Florida - east  
*   Escambia County, Florida - west

### Board of county commissioners
[edit]
The Santa Rosa County Board of County Commissioners serves as the legislative and policy-setting body of the county as established under Chapter 125 of the Florida Statutes. As such, the board enacts all legislation and authorizes programs and expenditures within the county. The board appoints a professionally trained county administrator, who is responsible for policy and budget development and implementation.
The board comprises five members, elected countywide. Members must reside within the particular districts for which they seek election. Each year, the board organizes itself, selecting a chair and vice chair from among its members to preside at commission meetings.

As of the 2020 census, 188,000 people, 69,454 households, and 47,876 families resided in the county.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
The median age was 40.3 years; 22.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 16.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 103.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 102.1 males age 18 and over.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### Racial and ethnic composition
The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% White, 5.9% Black or African American, 0.7% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.1% Asian, 0.2% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)
Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)
There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### Racial and ethnic composition
As of the 2000 census,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The population density was 116 inhabitants per square mile (45/km 2). The 49,119 housing units had an average density of 48 per square mile (19/km 2). The racial makeup of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% Native American, 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.
Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.
In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

### Racial and ethnic composition
The median income for a household in the county was $41,881 and for a family was $46,929. Males had a median income of $34,878 versus $22,304 for females. The per capita income for the county was $20,089. About 7.9% of families and 9.8% of the population were below the poverty line, including 12.6% of those under 18 and 7.5% of those 65 or over.
The Santa Rosa County Library System has five branches located in: Navarre, Gulf Breeze, Jay, Milton, and Pace.

**Navarre** is a census-designated place and unincorporated community in Santa Rosa County in the northwestern Florida Panhandle, United States. It is a major bedroom community for mostly U.S. military personnel, federal civil servants, local population, retirees and defense contractors. Due to Navarre Beach and the 4 miles (6.4 km) of beach front on the Gulf of Mexico thereof, as well as several miles of beaches within the Navarre Beach Marine Park and the Gulf Islands National Seashore, it has a small, but rapidly growing community of nature enthusiasts and tourists.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4) Navarre has grown from being a small town of around 1,500 in 1970 to a town with a population estimated at 43,540 as of 2022, if including both the Navarre and Navarre Beach Census Designated Places.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-Navarre_Census-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-NB_Census-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:26-7) The Navarre CDP recorded a population of 40,817 at the 2020 census.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-8)

Navarre is about 25 miles (40 km) east of Pensacola and about 15 miles (24 km) west of Fort Walton Beach. The community is roughly centered on the junction of U.S. Route 98 and State Road 87.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-towncenter-plan-9) It is part of the Pensacola–Ferry Pass–Brent, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area (more commonly referred to as the Pensacola Metro Area), and is the second largest community in the metropolitan area, according to a study.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10) Navarre is the third-largest community in the Florida Panhandle.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10)
Navarre is the principal community of the census-defined Navarre-Miramar Beach-Destin Urbanized Area. The community is known for the natural environment, swimming, picnic spots, and its beach.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4)
A busy day on Navarre Beach
In 1693, Spanish explorers Carlos de Sigüenza y Góngora and Admiral Andrés de Pez y Malzárraga became the first recorded Europeans to explore what is, today, Navarre. Sigüenza was responsible for scouting and mapping possible sites of Spanish colonization in Northwest Florida during the expedition. While traveling in the area of East Bay in April 1693 the Spanish discovered what is today called the East Bay River.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) In honor of Captain Jordan de Reina, an officer serving in the expedition, the Spanish dubbed the waters on which they traveled, "The River Jordan".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)

On April 11, 1693, while sailing up East Bay River, sailors aboard the Spanish ships noticed a group of Native Americans observing from a camp near the shore. In order to greet the natives, a landing party was sent out. By the time the Spanish reached the shore, however, the Native Americans were gone. As the Natives quickly abandoned camp the Spanish discovered half-cooked pieces of buffalo meat sitting over a fire, along with a fierce dog guarding the site. Due to the great number of oak trees in the area the campsite was named "El Robledal," meaning "The Oakgrove" in Spanish. Neighborhoods in the area of this event still retain the El Robledal name.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) After erecting a wooden cross and leaving gifts for the natives, the Spaniards continued their exploration upriver. Upon later return to El Robledal, the explorers noticed that their gifts had been taken. In return, the natives had also constructed a wooden cross and left a buffalo hide as a peace offering. The earliest known map of Robledal dates from 1693, the same year as the Pez-Sigüenza Expedition. Subsequent maps in 1698 continue to note the area today known as Navarre as Robledal.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
[edit]

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
[edit]
White settlers are noted as living in the area since at least 1827, when a map of West Florida includes listings of families by the name of Wyman and Williams living along Santa Rosa Sound in what would become Navarre. The Wyman family is believed to be related to Guy Wyman, who, along with his wife, would name the area "Navarre" and is now generally recognized as the town founder. The Williams family is likely the source of the name of [William's Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William's_Creek "William's Creek").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-13)
While various settlers had been present in the area since before this time, Robledal was again populated sometime near 1856, with the establishment of a homestead by the Axelson Family.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) Due to the relative lack of information on the other families, as well as their homestead's location at Robledal, they are often considered Navarre's first settlers. Their home was along the shore of the East Bay, on a small cape, in which, they are now the namesake, after the point was officially designated, Axelson Point.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-15)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
Soon after their settlement in what would become Navarre, they established a shipyard on Axelson Point, jutting into what was also then called, Axelson Cove.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12) The shipyard was considered to be mostly successful, as the family made a business of fixing ships in port in the nearby deep-water port in Pensacola and the river port in Milton, as well as building large-scale ships of their own.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) The shipyard was in operation until approximately 1890.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
During the Civil War, despite the political ideology of citizens in the area,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) records make it seem as though the Axelsons were pro-union. This is substantiated by a record showing that, while many businesses in the area were becoming ruined due to the Union blockade of southern ports, the Axelsons' shipyard was quite busy and prosperous, primarily from business completed with the Union navy and the United States Merchant Marines.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) This notion is conflicted with local tradition noted in _Log of the Peep O'Day_, an account of the area from the 1910s, which suggest that the Axelsons built one of the first ships registered under the flag of the Confederacy.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) However, as confirmed by evidence gathered by historians at the University of West Florida, this notion was likely caused by a confusion between the Axelsons and shipbuilding operations in nearby Milton.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)
In addition, some records and books, such as the _Atlas of Florida_, attest that Union raids were made against Confederate troops and camps stationed elsewhere in Northwest Florida, through routes in what would become Navarre and Holley.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-18) No evidence exists that the Axelsons assisted such missions. A military road that appears to approximate this route is noted as existing as late as 1895, where it can be found on War Department maps from that time period.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-19)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Bilowry and Hiawatha
[edit]
Some maps of the area during this time, seem to indicate that the area was also known as “Bilowry,” a presumed misspelling or combination of the name, Bill Lowry.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) The area also had a post office under this name from 1886 to 1891.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-21)
Habitation of this area of what is now Navarre was continuous, though sparse from the Axelsons to the platting of Navarre.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) This area also came to be known as Hiawatha during a brief time, with a neighborhood in Navarre still retaining this name.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-23)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Bilowry and Hiawatha
Some 30 years after the first homestead in the area was established, seemingly coinciding with the community of Bilowry, a small settlement named Eagan arose in 1874.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-24) The post office was run by Patrick Shea, a naturalized American from Ireland.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) The settlement, composed of approximately 40 families, was located off the Santa Rosa Sound and encompassed a portion of present-day Navarre. The settlement, which formerly existed as a post office location, was named after a local postmaster, John Eagan Esq., a Pensacola lawyer and politician.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) Following the post office's discontinuation on September 11, 1884, families continued to live in the area, and the town continued to appear on area maps even into the 1890s.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) While what became of the town and the people who lived there at that time is unknown (some of which are known to have remained in the town, some of which are believed to have moved to neighboring communities), the discovery of the town's existence definitively established the settlement of the Navarre area in South Santa Rosa County as being prior to the 20th century. The land upon which Eagan existed would, in fact, later become what is now known as Navarre.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25)

**Navarre** is a census-designated place and unincorporated community in Santa Rosa County in the northwestern Florida Panhandle, United States. It is a major bedroom community for mostly U.S. military personnel, federal civil servants, local population, retirees and defense contractors. Due to Navarre Beach and the 4 miles (6.4 km) of beach front on the Gulf of Mexico thereof, as well as several miles of beaches within the Navarre Beach Marine Park and the Gulf Islands National Seashore, it has a small, but rapidly growing community of nature enthusiasts and tourists.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4) Navarre has grown from being a small town of around 1,500 in 1970 to a town with a population estimated at 43,540 as of 2022, if including both the Navarre and Navarre Beach Census Designated Places.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-Navarre_Census-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-NB_Census-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:26-7) The Navarre CDP recorded a population of 40,817 at the 2020 census.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-8)
texts.3:
Navarre is about 25 miles (40 km) east of Pensacola and about 15 miles (24 km) west of Fort Walton Beach. The community is roughly centered on the junction of U.S. Route 98 and State Road 87.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-towncenter-plan-9) It is part of the Pensacola–Ferry Pass–Brent, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area (more commonly referred to as the Pensacola Metro Area), and is the second largest community in the metropolitan area, according to a study.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10) Navarre is the third-largest community in the Florida Panhandle.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10)
Navarre is the principal community of the census-defined Navarre-Miramar Beach-Destin Urbanized Area. The community is known for the natural environment, swimming, picnic spots, and its beach.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4)
A busy day on Navarre Beach
In 1693, Spanish explorers Carlos de Sigüenza y Góngora and Admiral Andrés de Pez y Malzárraga became the first recorded Europeans to explore what is, today, Navarre. Sigüenza was responsible for scouting and mapping possible sites of Spanish colonization in Northwest Florida during the expedition. While traveling in the area of East Bay in April 1693 the Spanish discovered what is today called the East Bay River.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) In honor of Captain Jordan de Reina, an officer serving in the expedition, the Spanish dubbed the waters on which they traveled, "The River Jordan".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)
texts.4: On April 11, 1693, while sailing up East Bay River, sailors aboard the Spanish ships noticed a group of Native Americans observing from a camp near the shore. In order to greet the natives, a landing party was sent out. By the time the Spanish reached the shore, however, the Native Americans were gone. As the Natives quickly abandoned camp the Spanish discovered half-cooked pieces of buffalo meat sitting over a fire, along with a fierce dog guarding the site. Due to the great number of oak trees in the area the campsite was named "El Robledal," meaning "The Oakgrove" in Spanish. Neighborhoods in the area of this event still retain the El Robledal name.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) After erecting a wooden cross and leaving gifts for the natives, the Spaniards continued their exploration upriver. Upon later return to El Robledal, the explorers noticed that their gifts had been taken. In return, the natives had also constructed a wooden cross and left a buffalo hide as a peace offering. The earliest known map of Robledal dates from 1693, the same year as the Pez-Sigüenza Expedition. Subsequent maps in 1698 continue to note the area today known as Navarre as Robledal.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)
texts.5:
### Axelson Point and early settlement
[edit]
texts.6:
### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
[edit]
White settlers are noted as living in the area since at least 1827, when a map of West Florida includes listings of families by the name of Wyman and Williams living along Santa Rosa Sound in what would become Navarre. The Wyman family is believed to be related to Guy Wyman, who, along with his wife, would name the area "Navarre" and is now generally recognized as the town founder. The Williams family is likely the source of the name of [William's Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William's_Creek "William's Creek").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-13)
While various settlers had been present in the area since before this time, Robledal was again populated sometime near 1856, with the establishment of a homestead by the Axelson Family.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) Due to the relative lack of information on the other families, as well as their homestead's location at Robledal, they are often considered Navarre's first settlers. Their home was along the shore of the East Bay, on a small cape, in which, they are now the namesake, after the point was officially designated, Axelson Point.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-15)
texts.7:
### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
Soon after their settlement in what would become Navarre, they established a shipyard on Axelson Point, jutting into what was also then called, Axelson Cove.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12) The shipyard was considered to be mostly successful, as the family made a business of fixing ships in port in the nearby deep-water port in Pensacola and the river port in Milton, as well as building large-scale ships of their own.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) The shipyard was in operation until approximately 1890.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)
texts.8:
### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
During the Civil War, despite the political ideology of citizens in the area,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) records make it seem as though the Axelsons were pro-union. This is substantiated by a record showing that, while many businesses in the area were becoming ruined due to the Union blockade of southern ports, the Axelsons' shipyard was quite busy and prosperous, primarily from business completed with the Union navy and the United States Merchant Marines.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) This notion is conflicted with local tradition noted in _Log of the Peep O'Day_, an account of the area from the 1910s, which suggest that the Axelsons built one of the first ships registered under the flag of the Confederacy.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) However, as confirmed by evidence gathered by historians at the University of West Florida, this notion was likely caused by a confusion between the Axelsons and shipbuilding operations in nearby Milton.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)
In addition, some records and books, such as the _Atlas of Florida_, attest that Union raids were made against Confederate troops and camps stationed elsewhere in Northwest Florida, through routes in what would become Navarre and Holley.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-18) No evidence exists that the Axelsons assisted such missions. A military road that appears to approximate this route is noted as existing as late as 1895, where it can be found on War Department maps from that time period.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-19)
texts.9:
### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Bilowry and Hiawatha
[edit]
Some maps of the area during this time, seem to indicate that the area was also known as “Bilowry,” a presumed misspelling or combination of the name, Bill Lowry.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) The area also had a post office under this name from 1886 to 1891.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-21)
Habitation of this area of what is now Navarre was continuous, though sparse from the Axelsons to the platting of Navarre.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) This area also came to be known as Hiawatha during a brief time, with a neighborhood in Navarre still retaining this name.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-23)
texts.10:
### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Bilowry and Hiawatha
Some 30 years after the first homestead in the area was established, seemingly coinciding with the community of Bilowry, a small settlement named Eagan arose in 1874.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-24) The post office was run by Patrick Shea, a naturalized American from Ireland.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) The settlement, composed of approximately 40 families, was located off the Santa Rosa Sound and encompassed a portion of present-day Navarre. The settlement, which formerly existed as a post office location, was named after a local postmaster, John Eagan Esq., a Pensacola lawyer and politician.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) Following the post office's discontinuation on September 11, 1884, families continued to live in the area, and the town continued to appear on area maps even into the 1890s.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) While what became of the town and the people who lived there at that time is unknown (some of which are known to have remained in the town, some of which are believed to have moved to neighboring communities), the discovery of the town's existence definitively established the settlement of the Navarre area in South Santa Rosa County as being prior to the 20th century. The land upon which Eagan existed would, in fact, later become what is now known as Navarre.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25)

**Navarre** is a census-designated place and unincorporated community in Santa Rosa County in the northwestern Florida Panhandle, United States. It is a major bedroom community for mostly U.S. military personnel, federal civil servants, local population, retirees and defense contractors. Due to Navarre Beach and the 4 miles (6.4 km) of beach front on the Gulf of Mexico thereof, as well as several miles of beaches within the Navarre Beach Marine Park and the Gulf Islands National Seashore, it has a small, but rapidly growing community of nature enthusiasts and tourists.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4) Navarre has grown from being a small town of around 1,500 in 1970 to a town with a population estimated at 43,540 as of 2022, if including both the Navarre and Navarre Beach Census Designated Places.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-Navarre_Census-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-NB_Census-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:26-7) The Navarre CDP recorded a population of 40,817 at the 2020 census.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-8)

Navarre is about 25 miles (40 km) east of Pensacola and about 15 miles (24 km) west of Fort Walton Beach. The community is roughly centered on the junction of U.S. Route 98 and State Road 87.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-towncenter-plan-9) It is part of the Pensacola–Ferry Pass–Brent, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area (more commonly referred to as the Pensacola Metro Area), and is the second largest community in the metropolitan area, according to a study.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10) Navarre is the third-largest community in the Florida Panhandle.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10)
Navarre is the principal community of the census-defined Navarre-Miramar Beach-Destin Urbanized Area. The community is known for the natural environment, swimming, picnic spots, and its beach.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4)
A busy day on Navarre Beach
In 1693, Spanish explorers Carlos de Sigüenza y Góngora and Admiral Andrés de Pez y Malzárraga became the first recorded Europeans to explore what is, today, Navarre. Sigüenza was responsible for scouting and mapping possible sites of Spanish colonization in Northwest Florida during the expedition. While traveling in the area of East Bay in April 1693 the Spanish discovered what is today called the East Bay River.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) In honor of Captain Jordan de Reina, an officer serving in the expedition, the Spanish dubbed the waters on which they traveled, "The River Jordan".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)

On April 11, 1693, while sailing up East Bay River, sailors aboard the Spanish ships noticed a group of Native Americans observing from a camp near the shore. In order to greet the natives, a landing party was sent out. By the time the Spanish reached the shore, however, the Native Americans were gone. As the Natives quickly abandoned camp the Spanish discovered half-cooked pieces of buffalo meat sitting over a fire, along with a fierce dog guarding the site. Due to the great number of oak trees in the area the campsite was named "El Robledal," meaning "The Oakgrove" in Spanish. Neighborhoods in the area of this event still retain the El Robledal name.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) After erecting a wooden cross and leaving gifts for the natives, the Spaniards continued their exploration upriver. Upon later return to El Robledal, the explorers noticed that their gifts had been taken. In return, the natives had also constructed a wooden cross and left a buffalo hide as a peace offering. The earliest known map of Robledal dates from 1693, the same year as the Pez-Sigüenza Expedition. Subsequent maps in 1698 continue to note the area today known as Navarre as Robledal.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
[edit]

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
[edit]
White settlers are noted as living in the area since at least 1827, when a map of West Florida includes listings of families by the name of Wyman and Williams living along Santa Rosa Sound in what would become Navarre. The Wyman family is believed to be related to Guy Wyman, who, along with his wife, would name the area "Navarre" and is now generally recognized as the town founder. The Williams family is likely the source of the name of [William's Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William's_Creek "William's Creek").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-13)
While various settlers had been present in the area since before this time, Robledal was again populated sometime near 1856, with the establishment of a homestead by the Axelson Family.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) Due to the relative lack of information on the other families, as well as their homestead's location at Robledal, they are often considered Navarre's first settlers. Their home was along the shore of the East Bay, on a small cape, in which, they are now the namesake, after the point was officially designated, Axelson Point.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-15)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
Soon after their settlement in what would become Navarre, they established a shipyard on Axelson Point, jutting into what was also then called, Axelson Cove.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12) The shipyard was considered to be mostly successful, as the family made a business of fixing ships in port in the nearby deep-water port in Pensacola and the river port in Milton, as well as building large-scale ships of their own.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) The shipyard was in operation until approximately 1890.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Settlement and shipyard
During the Civil War, despite the political ideology of citizens in the area,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) records make it seem as though the Axelsons were pro-union. This is substantiated by a record showing that, while many businesses in the area were becoming ruined due to the Union blockade of southern ports, the Axelsons' shipyard was quite busy and prosperous, primarily from business completed with the Union navy and the United States Merchant Marines.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) This notion is conflicted with local tradition noted in _Log of the Peep O'Day_, an account of the area from the 1910s, which suggest that the Axelsons built one of the first ships registered under the flag of the Confederacy.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) However, as confirmed by evidence gathered by historians at the University of West Florida, this notion was likely caused by a confusion between the Axelsons and shipbuilding operations in nearby Milton.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)
In addition, some records and books, such as the _Atlas of Florida_, attest that Union raids were made against Confederate troops and camps stationed elsewhere in Northwest Florida, through routes in what would become Navarre and Holley.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-18) No evidence exists that the Axelsons assisted such missions. A military road that appears to approximate this route is noted as existing as late as 1895, where it can be found on War Department maps from that time period.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-19)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Bilowry and Hiawatha
[edit]
Some maps of the area during this time, seem to indicate that the area was also known as “Bilowry,” a presumed misspelling or combination of the name, Bill Lowry.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) The area also had a post office under this name from 1886 to 1891.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-21)
Habitation of this area of what is now Navarre was continuous, though sparse from the Axelsons to the platting of Navarre.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) This area also came to be known as Hiawatha during a brief time, with a neighborhood in Navarre still retaining this name.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-23)

### Axelson Point and early settlement
#### Bilowry and Hiawatha
Some 30 years after the first homestead in the area was established, seemingly coinciding with the community of Bilowry, a small settlement named Eagan arose in 1874.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-24) The post office was run by Patrick Shea, a naturalized American from Ireland.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) The settlement, composed of approximately 40 families, was located off the Santa Rosa Sound and encompassed a portion of present-day Navarre. The settlement, which formerly existed as a post office location, was named after a local postmaster, John Eagan Esq., a Pensacola lawyer and politician.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) Following the post office's discontinuation on September 11, 1884, families continued to live in the area, and the town continued to appear on area maps even into the 1890s.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) While what became of the town and the people who lived there at that time is unknown (some of which are known to have remained in the town, some of which are believed to have moved to neighboring communities), the discovery of the town's existence definitively established the settlement of the Navarre area in South Santa Rosa County as being prior to the 20th century. The land upon which Eagan existed would, in fact, later become what is now known as Navarre.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25)

## Housing & Living
The median property value in Navarre, FL was $375,700 in 2024, which is 1.13 times larger than the national average of $332,700. Between 2023 and 2024 the median property value increased from $352,300 to $375,700, a 6.64% increase. The homeownership rate in Navarre, FL is 82.1%, which is higher than the national average of 65.2%.
People in Navarre, FL have an average commute time of 31.4 minutes, and they drove alone to work. Car ownership in Navarre, FL is approximately the same as the national average, with an average of 2 cars per household.

## About
None of the households in Pace, FL reported speaking a non-English language at home as their primary shared language. This does not consider the potential multi-lingual nature of households, but only the primary self-reported language spoken by all members of the household.
98.7% of the residents in Pace, FL are U.S. citizens.
In 2024, the median property value in Pace, FL was $293,800, and the homeownership rate was 83%.
Most people in Pace, FL drove alone to work, and the average commute time was 28.8 minutes. The average car ownership in Pace, FL was 2 cars per household.

**Santa Rosa County** is a county in the northwestern portion of the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The county seat is Milton, which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the Pensacola metropolitan area, which also includes Escambia County.

The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of Tristan de Luna's failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission serving Apalachees, Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in Floridatown from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)
Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint Rosa de Viterbo.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)
Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)
Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 1,174 square miles (3,040 km 2), of which 162 sq mi (420 km 2) (13.8%) are covered by water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR1-7)

### National protected area
[edit]
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part)
Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.
Navarre Beach
South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the Fairpoint Peninsula, and along U.S. Highway 98. A section of Santa Rosa Island, containing the unincorporated community of Navarre Beach, is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for Pensacola to the west and Hurlburt Field, Fort Walton Beach, and Eglin Air Force Base to the east.
Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called Old Spanish Trail that ran from St. Augustine to New Orleans, and further points west. Today, U.S. Highway 90 closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional Southern culture. The Pace and Milton communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. Interstate 10 also passes through this section of the county. The U.S. Navy presence is marked by Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.

### National protected area
Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along State Road 4, which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.
State Road 87 traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with Escambia County, Alabama, near Brewton, where it connects with State Route 41. This road is a primary emergency evacuation route for the county during hurricanes.
*   Escambia County, Alabama - north  
*   Okaloosa County, Florida - east  
*   Escambia County, Florida - west

### Board of county commissioners
[edit]
The Santa Rosa County Board of County Commissioners serves as the legislative and policy-setting body of the county as established under Chapter 125 of the Florida Statutes. As such, the board enacts all legislation and authorizes programs and expenditures within the county. The board appoints a professionally trained county administrator, who is responsible for policy and budget development and implementation.
The board comprises five members, elected countywide. Members must reside within the particular districts for which they seek election. Each year, the board organizes itself, selecting a chair and vice chair from among its members to preside at commission meetings.

The median age was 40.3 years; 22.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 16.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 103.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 102.1 males age 18 and over.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### Racial and ethnic composition
The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% White, 5.9% Black or African American, 0.7% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.1% Asian, 0.2% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)
Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)
There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

The racial makeup of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% Native American, 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.
Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.
In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

**Santa Rosa County** is a county in the northwestern portion of the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The county seat is Milton, which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the Pensacola metropolitan area, which also includes Escambia County.
texts.1:
The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of Tristan de Luna's failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission serving Apalachees, Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in Floridatown from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)
Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint Rosa de Viterbo.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)
Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)
Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 1,174 square miles (3,040 km 2), of which 162 sq mi (420 km 2) (13.8%) are covered by water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR1-7)
texts.2:
### National protected area
[edit]
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part)
Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.
Navarre Beach
South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the Fairpoint Peninsula, and along U.S. Highway 98. A section of Santa Rosa Island, containing the unincorporated community of Navarre Beach, is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for Pensacola to the west and Hurlburt Field, Fort Walton Beach, and Eglin Air Force Base to the east.
Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called Old Spanish Trail that ran from St. Augustine to New Orleans, and further points west. Today, U.S. Highway 90 closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional Southern culture. The Pace and Milton communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. Interstate 10 also passes through this section of the county. The U.S. Navy presence is marked by Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.
texts.3:
### National protected area
Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along State Road 4, which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.
State Road 87 traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with Escambia County, Alabama, near Brewton, where it connects with State Route 41. This road is a primary emergency evacuation route for the county during hurricanes.

### Board of county commissioners
[edit]
The Santa Rosa County Board of County Commissioners serves as the legislative and policy-setting body of the county as established under Chapter 125 of the Florida Statutes. As such, the board enacts all legislation and authorizes programs and expenditures within the county. The board appoints a professionally trained county administrator, who is responsible for policy and budget development and implementation.
The board comprises five members, elected countywide. Members must reside within the particular districts for which they seek election. Each year, the board organizes itself, selecting a chair and vice chair from among its members to preside at commission meetings.

texts.10:
### Racial and ethnic composition
The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% White, 5.9% Black or African American, 0.7% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.1% Asian, 0.2% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)
Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)
There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)
texts.11:
### Racial and ethnic composition
As of the 2000 census,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The population density was 116 inhabitants per square mile (45/km 2). The 49,119 housing units had an average density of 48 per square mile (19/km 2). The racial makeup of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% Native American, 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.
Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.
In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.
